verses.zh: 尼布甲尼撒王造了一个金像，高六十肘，宽六肘，立在巴比伦省杜拉平原。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] King Nebuchadnezzar had a golden[NOTE:2] statue made.[NOTE:3] It was 90 feet[NOTE:4] tall and 9 feet[NOTE:5] wide. He erected it on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.
notes: The LXX introduces this chapter with the following chronological note: “in the eighteenth year of.” Such a date would place these events at about the time of the destruction of Jerusalem in 586 b.c. (cf. 2 Kgs 25:8). However, there seems to be no real basis for associating the events of Daniel 3 with this date.

There is no need to think of Nebuchadnezzar’s image as being solid gold. No doubt the sense is that it was overlaid with gold (cf. Isa 40:19; Jer 10:3-4), with the result that it presented a dazzling self-compliment to the greatness of Nebuchadnezzar’s achievements.
According to a number of patristic authors, the image represented a deification of Nebuchadnezzar himself. This is not clear from the biblical text, however.
Aram “60 cubits.” Assuming a length of 18 inches for the standard cubit, the image would be 90 feet (27.4 m) high.

Aram “6 cubits.” Assuming a length of 18 inches for the standard cubit, the image would be 9 feet (2.74 m) wide.sn The dimensions of the image (90 feet high and 9 feet wide) imply that it did not possess normal human proportions, unless a base for the image is included in the height dimension. The ancient world knew of other tall statues. For example, the Colossus of Rhodes—the huge statue of Helios which stood (ca. 280-224 b.c.) at the entrance to the harbor at Rhodes and was one of the seven wonders of the ancient world—was said to be 70 cubits (105 ft or 32 m) in height, which would make it even taller than Nebuchadnezzar’s image.

verses.zh: 尼布甲尼撒王差人将总督、钦差、巡抚、臬司、藩司、谋士、法官，和各省的官员都召了来，为尼布甲尼撒王所立的像行开光之礼。
verses.en: Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent out a summons to assemble the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates,[NOTE:1] and all the other authorities of the province to attend the dedication of the statue that he[NOTE:2] had erected.
notes: The specific duties of the seven types of officials listed here (cf. vv. 3, 27) are unclear. The Aramaic words that are used are transliterations of Akkadian or Persian technical terms whose exact meanings are uncertain. The translations given here follow suggestions set forth in BDB.
Aram “Nebuchadnezzar the king.” The proper name and title have been replaced by the relative pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 于是总督、钦差、巡抚、臬司、藩司、谋士、法官，和各省的官员都聚集了来，要为尼布甲尼撒王所立的像行开光之礼，就站在尼布甲尼撒所立的像前。
verses.en: So the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the other provincial authorities assembled for the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had erected. They were standing in front of the statue that Nebuchadnezzar had erected.[NOTE:1]
notes: The LXX and Theodotion lack the words “that Nebuchadnezzar had erected.”

verses.zh: 那时传令的大声呼叫说：「各方、各国、各族（原文是舌：下同）的人哪，有令传与你们：
verses.en: Then the herald[NOTE:1] made a loud[NOTE:2] proclamation: “To you, O peoples, nations, and language groups, the following command is given:[NOTE:3]
notes: According to BDB 1097 s.v. כָּרוֹז the Aramaic word used here is a Greek loanword, but other scholars have argued instead for a Persian derivation (HALOT 1902 s.v. *כָּרוֹז).
Aram “in strength.”
Aram “they are saying.”

verses.zh: 你们一听见角、笛、琵琶、琴、瑟、笙，和各样乐器的声音，就当俯伏敬拜尼布甲尼撒王所立的金像。
verses.en: When you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither,[NOTE:1] trigon, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music, you must[NOTE:2] bow down and pay homage to the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has erected.
notes: The word zither (Aramaic קִיתָרוֹס [qitaros]), and the words for harp (Aramaic פְּסַנְתֵּרִין [pesanterin]) and pipes (Aramaic סוּמְפֹּנְיָה [sumponeyah]), are of Greek derivation. Though much has been made of this in terms of suggesting a date in the Hellenistic period for the writing of the book, it is not surprising that a few Greek cultural terms, all of them the names of musical instruments, should appear in this book. As a number of scholars have pointed out, the bigger surprise (if, in fact, the book is to be dated to the Hellenistic period) may be that there are so few Greek loanwords in Daniel.
The imperfect Aramaic verbs have here an injunctive nuance.

verses.zh: 凡不俯伏敬拜的，必立时扔在烈火的窑中。」
verses.en: Whoever does not bow down and pay homage will immediately[NOTE:1] be thrown into the midst of a furnace of blazing fire!”
notes: Aram “in that hour.”

verses.zh: 因此各方、各国、各族的人民一听见角、笛、琵琶、琴、瑟，和各样乐器的声音，就都俯伏敬拜尼布甲尼撒王所立的金像。
verses.en: Therefore when they all[NOTE:1] heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, trigon, harp, pipes,[NOTE:2] and all kinds of music, all the peoples, nations, and language groups began bowing down and paying homage to the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had erected.
notes: Aram “all the peoples.”
Though not in the Aramaic text of BHS, this word appears in many medieval Hebrew MSS, some LXX MSS, and the Vulgate (cf. vv. 5, 10, 15).

verses.zh: 那时，有几个迦勒底人进前来控告犹大人。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] at that time certain[NOTE:2] Chaldeans came forward and brought malicious accusations against[NOTE:3] the Jews.
notes: This expression is absent in Theodotion.
Aram “men.”
Aram “ate the pieces of.” This is a rather vivid idiom for slander.

verses.zh: 他们对尼布甲尼撒王说：「愿王万岁！
verses.en: They said[NOTE:1] to King Nebuchadnezzar, “O king, live forever![NOTE:2]
notes: Aram “answered and said,” a common Aramaic idiom that occurs repeatedly in this chapter.

O king, live forever! is a comment of typical court courtesy that is not necessarily indicative of the real sentiments of the speaker. Ancient oriental court protocol could sometimes require a certain amount of hypocrisy.

verses.zh: 王啊，你曾降旨说，凡听见角、笛、琵琶、琴、瑟、笙，和各样乐器声音的都当俯伏敬拜金像。
verses.en: You have issued an edict, O king, that everyone must bow down and pay homage to the golden statue when they hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, trigon, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music.

verses.zh: 凡不俯伏敬拜的，必扔在烈火的窑中。
verses.en: And whoever does not bow down and pay homage must be thrown into the midst of a furnace of blazing fire.

verses.zh: 现在有几个犹大人，就是王所派管理巴比伦省事务的沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌；王啊，这些人不理你，不事奉你的神，也不敬拜你所立的金像。」
verses.en: But there are Jewish men whom you appointed over the administration of the province of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—and these men[NOTE:1] have not shown proper respect to you, O king. They don’t serve your gods, and they don’t pay homage to the golden statue that you have erected.”
notes: Daniel’s absence from this scene has sparked the imagination of commentators, some of whom have suggested that perhaps he was unable to attend the dedication due to sickness or absence prompted by business. Hippolytus supposed that Daniel may have been watching from a distance.

verses.zh: 当时，尼布甲尼撒冲冲大怒，吩咐人把沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌带过来，他们就把那些人带到王面前。
verses.en: Then Nebuchadnezzar in a fit of rage[NOTE:1] demanded that they bring[NOTE:2] Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego before him. So they brought them[NOTE:3] before the king.
notes: Aram “in anger and wrath”; NASB “in rage and anger.” The expression is a hendiadys.
The Aramaic infinitive is active.
Aram “these men.” The pronoun is used in the translation to avoid undue repetition.

verses.zh: 尼布甲尼撒问他们说：「沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌，你们不事奉我的神，也不敬拜我所立的金像，是故意的吗？
verses.en: Nebuchadnezzar said to them, “Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you don’t serve my gods and that you don’t pay homage to the golden statue that I erected?

verses.zh: 你们再听见角、笛、琵琶、琴、瑟、笙，和各样乐器的声音，若俯伏敬拜我所造的像，却还可以；若不敬拜，必立时扔在烈火的窑中，有何神能救你们脱离我手呢？」
verses.en: Now if you are ready, when you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, trigon, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music, you must bow down and pay homage to the statue that I had made. If you don’t pay homage to it, you will immediately be thrown into the midst of the furnace of blazing fire. Now, who is that god who can rescue you from my power?”[NOTE:1]
notes: Aram “hand,” as also in v. 17.

verses.zh: 沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌对王说：「尼布甲尼撒啊，这件事我们不必回答你；
verses.en: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego replied to King Nebuchadnezzar,[NOTE:1] “We do not need to give you a reply[NOTE:2] concerning this.
notes: In the MT this word is understood to begin the following address (“answered and said to the king, ‘O Nebuchadnezzar’”). However, it seems unlikely that Nebuchadnezzar’s subordinates would address the king in such a familiar way, particularly in light of the danger that they now found themselves in. The present translation implies moving the verse-dividing atnakh from “king” to “Nebuchadnezzar.”
Aram “to return a word to you.”

verses.zh: 即便如此，我们所事奉的　神能将我们从烈火的窑中救出来。王啊，他也必救我们脱离你的手；
verses.en: If[NOTE:1] our God whom we are serving exists,[NOTE:2] he is able to rescue us from the furnace of blazing fire, and he will rescue us, O king, from your power as well.
notes: The ancient versions typically avoid the conditional element of v. 17.

The Aramaic expression used here is very difficult to interpret. The question concerns the meaning and syntax of אִיתַי (ʾitay, “is” or “exist”). There are several possibilities. (1) Some interpreters take this word closely with the participle later in the verse יָכִל (yakhil, “able”), understanding the two words to form a periphrastic construction (“if our God is…able”; cf. H. Bauer and P. Leander, Grammatik des Biblisch-Aramäischen, 365, §111b). But the separation of the two elements from one another is not an argument in favor of this understanding. (2) Other interpreters take the first part of v. 17 to mean “If it is so, then our God will deliver us” (cf. KJV, ASV, RSV, NASB). However, the normal sense of ʾitay is existence; on this point see F. Rosenthal, Grammar, 41, §95. The present translation maintains the sense of existence for the verb (“If our God…exists”), even though the statement is admittedly difficult to understand in this light. The statement may be an implicit reference back to Nebuchadnezzar’s comment in v. 15, which denies the existence of a god capable of delivering from the king’s power, thus their statement is rhetorically adapted to the perspective of the person they are addressing.

verses.zh: 即或不然，王啊，你当知道我们决不事奉你的神，也不敬拜你所立的金像。」
verses.en: But if he does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we don’t serve your gods, and we will not pay homage to the golden statue that you have erected.”

verses.zh: 当时，尼布甲尼撒怒气填胸，向沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌变了脸色，吩咐人把窑烧热，比寻常更加七倍；
verses.en: Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with rage, and his disposition changed[NOTE:1] toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He gave orders[NOTE:2] to heat the furnace seven times hotter than it was normally heated.
notes: Aram “the appearance of his face was altered”; cf. NLT “his face became distorted with rage”; NAB “[his] face became livid with utter rage.”
Aram “he answered and said.”

verses.zh: 又吩咐他军中的几个壮士，将沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌捆起来，扔在烈火的窑中。
verses.en: He ordered strong[NOTE:1] soldiers in his army to tie up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and to throw them into the furnace of blazing fire.
notes: This is sometimes taken as a comparative: “[some of the] strongest.”

verses.zh: 这三人穿着裤子、内袍、外衣，和别的衣服，被捆起来扔在烈火的窑中。
verses.en: So those men were tied up while still wearing their cloaks, trousers, turbans, and other clothes,[NOTE:1] and were thrown into the furnace[NOTE:2] of blazing fire.
notes: There is a great deal of uncertainty with regard to the specific nature of these items of clothing.
Aram “into the midst of the furnace.” For stylistic reasons the words “the midst of” have been left untranslated.

verses.zh: 因为王命紧急，窑又甚热，那抬沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌的人都被火焰烧死。
verses.en: But since the king’s command was so urgent, and the furnace was so excessively hot, the men who escorted[NOTE:1] Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego were killed[NOTE:2] by the leaping flames.[NOTE:3]
notes: Aram “caused to go up.”
The Aramaic verb is active.
Aram “the flame of the fire” (so KJV, ASV, NASB); NRSV “the raging flames.”

verses.zh: 沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌这三个人都被捆着落在烈火的窑中。
verses.en: But those three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell into the furnace[NOTE:1] of blazing fire while still securely bound.[NOTE:2]
notes: Aram “into the midst of the furnace.” For stylistic reasons the words “the midst of” have been left untranslated.

The deuterocanonical writings known as The Prayer of Azariah and The Song of the Three present at this point a confession and petition for God’s forgiveness and a celebration of God’s grace for the three Jewish youths in the fiery furnace. Though not found in the Hebrew/Aramaic text of Daniel, these compositions do appear in the ancient Greek versions.

verses.zh: 那时，尼布甲尼撒王惊奇，急忙起来，对谋士说：「我捆起来扔在火里的不是三个人吗？」他们回答王说：「王啊，是。」
verses.en: Then King Nebuchadnezzar was startled and quickly got up. He said to his ministers, “Wasn’t it three men that we tied up and threw[NOTE:1] into[NOTE:2] the fire?” They replied to the king, “For sure, O king.”
notes: Aram “we threw…bound.”
Aram “into the midst of.”

verses.zh: 王说：「看哪，我见有四个人，并没有捆绑，在火中游行，也没有受伤；那第四个的相貌好像神子。」
verses.en: He answered, “But I see four men, untied and walking around in the midst of the fire! No harm has come to them! And the appearance of the fourth is like that of a god!”[NOTE:1]
notes: The phrase like that of a god is in Aramaic “like that of a son of the gods.” Many patristic writers understood this phrase in a christological sense (i.e., “the Son of God”). But it should be remembered that these are words spoken by a pagan who is seeking to explain things from his own polytheistic frame of reference; for him the phrase “like a son of the gods” is equivalent to “like a divine being.” Despite the king’s description though, the fourth person probably was an angel who had come to deliver the three men, or was a theophany.

verses.zh: 于是，尼布甲尼撒就近烈火窑门，说：「至高　神的仆人沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌出来，上这里来吧！」沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌就从火中出来了。
verses.en: Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the door of the furnace of blazing fire. He called out,[NOTE:1] “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the most high God, come out! Come here!” Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego emerged from the fire.[NOTE:2]
notes: Aram “answered and said.”
Aram “from the midst of the fire.” For stylistic reasons the words “the midst of” have been left untranslated.

verses.zh: 那些总督、钦差、巡抚，和王的谋士一同聚集看这三个人，见火无力伤他们的身体，头发也没有烧焦，衣裳也没有变色，并没有火燎的气味。
verses.en: Once the satraps, prefects, governors, and ministers of the king had gathered around, they saw that those men were physically[NOTE:1] unharmed by the fire.[NOTE:2] The hair of their heads was not singed, nor were their trousers damaged. Not even the smell of fire was to be found on them!
notes: Aram “in their bodies.”
Aram “the fire did not have power.”

verses.zh: 尼布甲尼撒说：「沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌的　神是应当称颂的！他差遣使者救护倚靠他的仆人，他们不遵王命，舍去己身，在他们　神以外不肯事奉敬拜别神。
verses.en: Nebuchadnezzar exclaimed,[NOTE:1] “Praised be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent forth his angel[NOTE:2] and has rescued his servants who trusted in him, ignoring[NOTE:3] the edict of the king and giving up their bodies rather than[NOTE:4] serve or pay homage to any god other than their God!
notes: Aram “answered and said.”

The king identifies the “son of the gods” (v. 25) as an angel. Comparable Hebrew expressions are used elsewhere in the Hebrew Bible for the members of God’s angelic assembly (see Gen 6:2, 4; Job 1:6; 2:1; 38:7; Pss 29:1; 89:6). An angel later comes to rescue Daniel from the lions (Dan 6:22).
Aram “they changed” or “violated.”
Aram “so that they might not.”

verses.zh: 现在我降旨，无论何方、何国、何族的人，谤讟沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌之　神的，必被凌迟，他的房屋必成粪堆，因为没有别神能这样施行拯救。」
verses.en: I hereby decree[NOTE:1] that any people, nation, or language group that blasphemes[NOTE:2] the God of Shadrach, Meshach, or Abednego will be dismembered and his home reduced to rubble! For there exists no other god who can deliver in this way.”
notes: Aram “from me is placed an edict.”
Aram “speaks negligence.”

verses.zh: 那时王在巴比伦省，高升了沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌。
verses.en: Then Nebuchadnezzar[NOTE:1] promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
notes: Aram “and the king.” The proper name has been supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
